title: Columbia Grant - International Undergraduate Need-Based Financial Aid
program_type: Need-based institutional financial aid assessed annually against the full cost of attendance; Columbia awards no merit scholarships
funding_type: Need-based institutional grant (Columbia Grant) plus student employment; loans are never used to meet need
administering_authority: Columbia University - Financial Aid & Educational Financing, 618 Lerner Hall, 2920 Broadway, New York, NY 10027; 212-854-3711; ugrad-finaid@columbia.edu
implementing_agency: Columbia University - Financial Aid & Educational Financing, for Columbia College and Columbia Engineering (The Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science)
programme_action: Columbia University need-based financial aid programme for international first-year applicants, principally the Columbia Grant, administered by Financial Aid & Educational Financing alongside the Office of Undergraduate Admissions application
description: Columbia University meets 100% of the demonstrated financial need of every admitted first-year student regardless of citizenship, for all four years of study. All aid is need-based: Columbia states there are no academic, athletic or talent-based institutional scholarships at Columbia College and Columbia Engineering. International applicants are evaluated in a need-aware admissions process and must declare themselves financial aid applicants on the admission application, because an international student admitted without an aid request can never apply for aid later. International students are not eligible for federal student aid, so their need is met entirely from institutional resources. The average award for international financial aid recipients is $79,375, usually comprising a Columbia Grant that does not need to be repaid and a student work-study job; loans are not included in aid packages. The aid application itself is the CSS Profile with parental tax returns or income documentation submitted through College Board's IDOC, which is separate from and submitted after the admission application.

award_types: Columbia Grant - need-based funding provided by the University that does not need to be repaid
Student Employment - the term-time work expectation that forms part of the aid award (on-campus work, averaging about 7 hours a week)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: Financial Aid & Educational Financing states that all aid it administers is need-based and that there are no academic, athletic or talent-based institutional scholarships. Federal grants (Pell Grant, Supplemental Education Opportunity Grant) and the New York State Tuition Assistance Program are determined by the FAFSA and are not available to international students, so international need is met entirely from institutional resources. The $2,000 start-up grant for incoming first-year students from low-income families is a one-time transition payment rather than a recurring award. Course fee waivers are awarded automatically to students receiving the Columbia Grant for most courses, excluding physical education courses.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Columbia conducts a thorough financial analysis for each student every academic year and continues to meet 100% of demonstrated need for all four years of study for students admitted as financial aid applicants. Renewal is therefore a re-assessment of need rather than a performance condition; no GPA or credit threshold is published. The decisive rule is at entry: an international student must indicate financial aid applicant status on the admissions application, because international financial aid cannot be awarded in subsequent years if it was not awarded at the time of admission, and an international student admitted without institutional aid may not apply for it at any time during enrolment unless citizenship status changes (a severe, unforeseen change in family circumstances may be reviewed case by case).
programme_structure.intake: Fall entry only, for first-year applicants to Columbia College or Columbia Engineering. Transfer and Combined Plan applicants use separate processes; Columbia guarantees full demonstrated need for transfer students pursuing their first degree on the same need-based basis.

The logo asset was verified by direct HTTP request returning image/png bytes on the official cc-seas.financialaid.columbia.edu domain.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Application opens 1 August. Early Decision and QuestBridge National College Match application deadline 1 November; Early Decision financial aid application deadline 15 November 2026; Early Decision admissions and financial aid decisions released mid-December; Regular Decision application deadline 1 January 2027; Regular Decision financial aid application deadline 15 February 2027; Regular Decision admissions and financial aid decisions released late March; Regular Decision response deadline 1 May.
application_deadline.application_period: 2026-2027 admissions cycle, for first-year entry in Fall 2027
application_deadline.official_rule: The financial aid deadline is round-specific and is published with an exact calendar date on the office's application policy pages: Sunday, November 15, 2026 for Early Decision international applicants and Monday, February 15, 2027 for Regular Decision international applicants. The admission application deadlines are 1 November (Early Decision and QuestBridge) and 1 January (Regular Decision). Columbia states that financial aid materials received after the deadline will be processed without penalty but may delay the financial aid evaluation, and that supporting documentation from schools may arrive after the deadline without an extension. No submission time or timezone is published for the aid deadlines, so none is recorded.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: The critical rule is not the aid paperwork date but the declaration on the admission application: international students must indicate their request for financial aid when submitting their admission application and cannot change the request afterwards. A student offered admission who did not apply for financial aid will not be able to change that status at any point. Because Columbia publishes cycle dates as 'based on typical admissions cycles', re-verify each date before the November and January rounds.

programme_duration.official_range: Bachelor's degree at Columbia College or Columbia Engineering, typically eight semesters (approximately four years) of full-time study
programme_duration.renewal_note: Columbia states it meets 100% of demonstrated financial need for all four years of study for students admitted as financial aid applicants, and re-analyses each family's finances every academic year. Renewal therefore depends on continued demonstrated need and on the student having been admitted as an aid applicant, not on maintaining a grade threshold.

funding.scholarship_type: Need-based institutional grant (Columbia Grant) plus a term-time student employment expectation; loans are not used to meet need and no merit scholarships exist
funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly stipend or allowance is published. Aid is an annual award of a Columbia Grant plus student employment assessed against the cost of attendance. The only separately published payment is the one-time $2,000 start-up grant for incoming first-year students from low-income families.
funding.travel_amount_note: Travel and local transportation is a variable allowance line in the cost of attendance ('varies'). Columbia's published examples are $944 for a student from Indiana and $1,254 from California, and the allowance accounts for two round-trip flights, with higher amounts for students whose country of residence is further from New York City.
funding.institutional_costs: The Columbia Grant is applied against the full 2026-2027 cost of attendance: tuition $72,800; fees $4,160 (including one-time transcript and orientation fees of $730 in the first semester); food $7,128; housing $12,522; books and supplies $1,320; personal expenses $1,844; travel and local transportation varies. The first-year on-campus total budget is $99,774 and the continuing on-campus total is $100,884. The International Services Charge of $175 per semester, charged to international students, is included in the cost of attendance for those students. Columbia Health Insurance ($2,218 Fall term, $3,605 Spring term) is not included in the cost of attendance.
funding.fully_funded_note: Columbia meets 100% of demonstrated need, and for families with calculated incomes below $66,000 (with typical assets) the parent contribution is $0, with the summer-earnings portion of the student contribution waived for first-year students in that position. The record does not set fully_funded true because coverage is individually assessed rather than universal, because every aid recipient is still expected to meet a Student Responsibility (a Student Contribution of at least $2,400 for most incoming first-year students plus a term-time work expectation averaging about 7 hours a week), because the award must be requested at admission and cannot be added later, and because Columbia Health Insurance sits outside the cost of attendance. The university's own framing is that students are expected to borrow $0, not that attendance is free.

tuition.amount: Up to the full 2026-2027 tuition of $72,800, set by demonstrated need
tuition.conditions: Columbia meets 100% of demonstrated need for all admitted students regardless of citizenship. Families with calculated total incomes below $66,000 (and typical assets) have a $0 expected parent contribution; families with calculated incomes between $66,000 and $150,000 (and typical assets) are able to attend tuition-free; families earning upwards of $100,000, and as much as about $250,000, can also qualify for need-based aid. There are no income or asset cutoffs, and the median income of families receiving the Columbia Grant is $96,229.

monthly_stipend.note: No monthly stipend or living allowance is published. The award is an annual grant assessed against the cost of attendance, which itself contains standard allowances for housing, food, books, personal expenses and travel.

travel_allowance.note: Travel and local transportation is an allowance line in the cost of attendance and is covered within the need package. The allowance varies by distance from New York City; Columbia's published examples are $944 for a student from Indiana and $1,254 from California.

installation_allowance.note: Incoming first-year students from low-income families receive a $2,000 start-up grant to ease their transition to college. It is a one-time payment, not a recurring allowance.

visa_support.note: No visa or immigration fee support is published. International student immigration matters are handled by the International Students & Scholars Office (isso.columbia.edu), which is referenced as a related service rather than as a funder.

insurance.note: Health insurance is not included in the cost of attendance. Students who remain on Columbia Health Insurance are charged $2,218 for the Fall term and $3,605 for the Spring term; a waiver may be requested from mid-July to the end of September for students with comparable coverage, and enrolled students may ask for the fees to be included in their cost of attendance to assist with awarding work-study or loan funds.

research_allowance.note: No research allowance is published for entering students. Enrolled students may access the Work Exemption Program and additional funding for unpaid research, internship and community service opportunities, plus enhanced aid for study abroad during the academic year; these apply after enrolment, not at entry.

book_allowance.note: Books and supplies are a $1,320 allowance line in the 2026-2027 cost of attendance and are covered within the need-based award.

equipment_allowance.note: No equipment allowance is published. Course fees vary by course, and automatic course fee waivers are awarded to students receiving the Columbia Grant for most courses, excluding physical education courses.

family_allowance.note: No family or dependent allowance is published as standard. Students with dependents may request that dependent care expenses be included in their cost of attendance.

accommodation_support.note: Housing ($12,522) and food ($7,128) are allowance lines in the 2026-2027 cost of attendance and are covered within the need package. First-year students are required to live on campus; non-first-year housing is based on the standard room charge and the Meal Plan EZ 19, and upperclassmen living off campus receive the same allowance.

bond.note: No service bond or repayment obligation is published. The Columbia Grant is need-based funding that does not need to be repaid, loans are not used to meet need, and Columbia states students are expected to borrow $0 to attend.

total_estimated_value.note: The award is individually calculated against demonstrated need, so no fixed total is published. Published averages: $79,375 average award for international financial aid recipients (usually a Columbia Grant plus a student work-study job), $76,503 average first-year grants and scholarships across all first-year students, and $70,797 average Columbia grant among Columbia College and Columbia Engineering students, 51% of whom receive grants from Columbia.

coverage: Tuition, fees, housing, food, books and supplies, personal expenses and a travel allowance - the full 2026-2027 cost of attendance of $99,774 for a first-year on-campus student - up to 100% of demonstrated financial need
A Columbia Grant, which is need-based funding provided by the University that does not need to be repaid
Term-time student employment forming part of the award, with work-study recipients earning wages in an on-campus job averaging about 7 hours a week
Annual renewal for all four years of study for students admitted as financial aid applicants
A one-time $2,000 start-up grant for incoming first-year students from low-income families
Automatic course fee waivers for most courses for students receiving the Columbia Grant, excluding physical education courses
coverage_limitations: Aid is need-based and individually calculated; there is no published fixed amount, and the $79,375, $76,503 and $70,797 figures are averages rather than entitlements.
All financial aid at Columbia is need-based - there are no academic, athletic or talent-based institutional merit scholarships, so a strong academic record alone never produces an award.

International students are not eligible for federal student aid (FAFSA, Pell Grant, Supplemental Education Opportunity Grant) or New York State TAP; their need is met entirely from institutional resources.
Admission is need-aware for international applicants, so the admissions committee takes how much aid a student requires into account when rendering a decision.
The aid request must be indicated on the admission application and cannot be changed after submission; international financial aid cannot be awarded in later years if it was not awarded at admission.

Every aid recipient is expected to meet a Student Responsibility: a Student Contribution with a minimum of $2,400 for most incoming first-year students (summer earnings, waived for first-year students with a $0 parent contribution, with any student-assets portion still applying) plus a term-time work expectation.
Columbia Health Insurance ($2,218 Fall, $3,605 Spring) is not part of the cost of attendance and must be paid or waived with comparable insurance.
Travel and local transportation is a variable allowance rather than a fixed sum, and is larger for students residing further from New York City.
Financial aid materials received after the deadline are processed without penalty but may delay the financial aid evaluation.
International applicants requesting aid who apply Early Decision may be deferred to Regular Decision so the committee can review the entire global applicant pool.
eligible_applicants: International applicants - students who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents, do not hold refugee visas or asylum status, and are not undocumented - applying as first-year students to Columbia College or Columbia Engineering
U.S. citizens, eligible noncitizens, DACA recipients and undocumented students, who are served by the same programme under need-blind admission
Applicants from any country and any secondary school curriculum, applying for full-time Fall 2027 entry
final_year_condition: Not applicable in the bachelor's-completion sense. The award funds entry INTO a bachelor's degree. Applicants must be completing secondary school, and Columbia reviews all secondary school curricula in context: internal and external examination results (A Level, International Baccalaureate, French Baccalaureate, Advanced Placement and other final national examinations) must be submitted where they are required to complete and graduate from secondary school.
equivalent_degree_note: Columbia accepts all secondary school curricula, including International Baccalaureate, Cambridge A Levels and national school curricula, and reviews each application within the context of the applicant's curriculum. Staff have read applications from school systems worldwide and may contact the school or conduct their own research if more information is needed. Columbia also states that it does not authorize or work with any independent agents anywhere in the world for recruitment.

age_limit.official_source: No age limit is published for first-year admission or for financial aid on any official Columbia page read for this record.

eligibility.citizenship: Open to applicants of any citizenship. For financial aid purposes, students who are not citizens or permanent residents of the United States, do not have refugee visas or asylum status, and are not undocumented are considered international. The same need-based programme serves domestic applicants, whose admission is need-blind, and international applicants, whose admission is need-aware.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No residence requirement. Applicants may apply from a secondary school in any country, and applications are reviewed by region with a school profile describing the school, grading system, curriculum and extracurricular resources.
eligibility.age_limit: No age minimum or maximum is published on the official pages reviewed.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Completion of secondary school in any curriculum. Columbia College strongly recommends four years of English literature and composition, four years of mathematics, three to four years of history and/or social studies, three to four years of laboratory science and three to four years of one world language. Columbia Engineering strongly advises four years of mathematics through calculus, four years of laboratory science including one year of chemistry and one year of physics, four years of English literature and composition, three to four years of history and two to three years of a world language.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Holistic admission review with no published GPA or score threshold. Applicants to enter in Fall 2027 may choose whether or not to submit SAT or ACT testing; Columbia will require standardized test scores for the 2027-2028 admissions cycle and beyond.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: HOLISTIC - no minimum GPA, class rank or score threshold is published for admission or for aid. Selection is through the holistic admissions review described on the Understanding the Process pages.
eligibility.language_requirement: Demonstration of English language proficiency is required for applicants who do not meet one of Columbia's exemption criteria; the specific minimums are recorded in the english_requirement block.
eligibility.work_experience: No work experience requirement is published. Employment and summer activities are described in the application as material for the holistic review.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: No formal requirement is published; the application collects lists and descriptions of achievements, activities, employment and summer activities.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Not published as a formal requirement for admission or for aid.
eligibility.financial_need: Demonstrated financial need is the sole basis of the award. Eligibility is determined by evaluating the family's ability to pay, considering total income including untaxed income, parent assets (cash, savings, investments, home equity, other real estate equity and business equity, with retirement assets excluded), household size and expenses, the number of siblings enrolled in undergraduate programmes, and special circumstances documented in the Special Circumstances section of the CSS Profile or in a letter to the office.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: No restriction on holding a previous scholarship is published. Outside scholarships are applied to replace, dollar for dollar, the Student Contribution and work-expectation components of the award; once those are exceeded the excess reduces the Columbia Grant, and outside scholarships never reduce the parent contribution.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Full-time enrolment at Columbia College or Columbia Engineering. Aid eligibility is re-analysed every academic year, and first-year students are required to live on campus.
eligibility.health_requirement: No health requirement is published as a condition of aid. Columbia Health Insurance is charged separately from the cost of attendance unless waived with comparable coverage.
eligibility.field_restrictions: No field-of-study restriction. The programme covers Columbia College and Columbia Engineering (The Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science) across all majors; applicants to Columbia Engineering must have one of their two teacher recommendations come from a math or science teacher.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No GPA, percentage or standardised score threshold is published for admission or for aid; admission is holistic. Columbia is test-optional for Fall 2027 entrants and will require testing from the 2027-2028 cycle onwards.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Two teacher recommendations from teachers who taught the applicant in academic disciplines (for Columbia Engineering, one must be from a math or science teacher); a Secondary School Report completed by a school counselor or other school official containing an official transcript from all high schools attended, one counselor recommendation and school profile, and the completed midyear report; responses to the Columbia-specific application questions; a personal essay; and, for non-native English speakers, demonstration of English proficiency.
selection_factors_may_include: Strength of the secondary school academic record within the context of the applicant's curriculum and school system
Rigour of the completed programme, including IB, A Levels, French Baccalaureate, AP and national curricula
Internal and external examination results where required to complete secondary school
Columbia-specific application responses demonstrating intellectual curiosity, habits of mind and love of learning
Achievements, activities, employment and summer activities
Two teacher recommendations and the counselor recommendation with school profile
Optional standardised testing (SAT or ACT) for Fall 2027 applicants
Optional supplementary materials such as an arts portfolio, research abstract or resume
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Columbia reviews each application holistically and with care, with the stated goal of identifying applicants who will make the most of the Columbia experience. No rubric, weighting or cut-off is published for admission or for aid, so none is recorded. Interviews are explicitly not part of the application process, per the May 2023 announcement ending alumni admissions interviews.

english_requirement.moi_rule: No exam is required if the applicant's home language is English; if the primary language of instruction at school has been English for the duration of the secondary school career; or if the applicant earned 700 or higher on the Reading and Writing section of the SAT (paper or digital) or 29 or higher on the English or Reading sections of the ACT.
english_requirement.test_score_note: The published figures are stated minimums, not ranges. TOEFL: a minimum of 105 on the internet-based test for exams taken on or before 20 January 2026, and a minimum of 5.5 for exams taken on or after 21 January 2026, reflecting the new TOEFL score scale; scores must be reported directly by the testing service using report code 2116. IELTS: 7.5 on IELTS Academic or IELTS Academic for UKVI. Duolingo English Test: 135 on the current DET. Cambridge English: 191 on the current C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency. Columbia accepts only full TOEFL iBT test administration results and does not accept MyBest scores; the TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition is accepted. PTE Academic is not among the accepted tests. Applicants may optionally send InitialView or Vericant conversational videos (by 15 November for Early Decision, 15 January for Regular Decision), which support the fluency assessment but do not replace an exam.
accepted_tests: TOEFL internet-Based Test (iBT), including the TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition

language_of_instruction.language_note: All Columbia College and Columbia Engineering bachelor's programmes are taught in English, and Columbia requires applicants to be comfortable with rapid and idiomatic spoken English. Any application documents not issued in English, such as transcripts or recommendations, must be officially translated into English and submitted with the originals.

application_method.application_route: Two separate submissions. First, the admission application through the Common Application, the Coalition Application on Scoir, or the QuestBridge Application for QuestBridge Finalists, on which the international applicant must indicate that they are a financial aid applicant. Second, the financial aid application itself: the CSS Profile, with parental tax returns or income documentation submitted through College Board's Institutional Documentation Service (IDOC). The aid application is separate from, and submitted after, the admission application.
application_steps: Submit the Common Application, Coalition Application on Scoir or QuestBridge Application, including the autobiographical information, activities lists, personal essay and Columbia-specific application questions, by 1 November (Early Decision and QuestBridge National College Match) or 1 January (Regular Decision), indicating on the application that you are a financial aid applicant.
Pay or waive the $85 nonrefundable application fee at submission; fee waiver eligibility can be checked in advance through Columbia's fee waiver form.

Have your school submit the Secondary School Report with an official transcript from all high schools attended, one counselor recommendation, the school profile and the midyear report; two teacher recommendations are required, with one from a math or science teacher for Columbia Engineering applicants.
Ensure any non-English documents are officially translated into English and submitted with the originals.
Submit the CSS Profile to determine eligibility for institutional aid including the Columbia University Grant.

Upload or mail parental tax returns and income documentation to College Board's IDOC after receiving the IDOC instruction email that follows the CSS Profile submission; electronic upload is strongly advised and documents generally reach Columbia within 3-5 business days.
Track document status in the Columbia Online Financial Aid System and respond promptly to any requests for additional materials.
Low-income international students may request a CSS Profile fee waiver by contacting ugrad-finaid@columbia.edu.
Await the admissions and financial aid decision, released together: mid-December for Early Decision and late March for Regular Decision.

selection_process.decision_maker: Columbia University Office of Undergraduate Admissions (Committee on Admissions) for admission; Financial Aid & Educational Financing determines the aid award after admission
selection_process.selection_type: Need-based award determined by a financial analysis of the family's ability to pay, conducted after the admissions decision; there is no separate scholarship competition, interview or committee
possible_stages: Admission application completeness review, including transcripts, school report, recommendations and English proficiency
Holistic admissions review; for international applicants this review is need-aware and considers the aid request
Admissions decision released with the financial aid decision (mid-December for Early Decision, late March for Regular Decision)

Financial aid analysis of the CSS Profile and IDOC documentation: parent contribution from income, assets, household size, number in college and special circumstances; student contribution and work expectation
Award issued as a Columbia Grant plus student employment, with no loans, meeting 100% of demonstrated need
Annual re-analysis for each of the four years of study
selection_process.weighting_note: No rubric or weighting is published for admission or for aid. The aid formula is published in structural terms only: Parent Contribution plus Student Responsibility equals Net Cost, and grant assistance covers the full difference between that net cost and the cost of attendance.
selection_process.results_timing: Admissions and financial aid decisions are released together: mid-December for Early Decision and late March for Regular Decision, with the Early Decision reply deadline in mid-January and the Regular Decision reply deadline on 1 May. Decisions are released only through the applicant portal, never by email.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: Columbia does not publish a ranked list, an award distribution or a number of international aid recipients. It publishes that it admits a large number of international students who receive a substantial amount of financial aid, that international aid totalled $19 million in 2023-2024, and that $21 million is currently awarded in international financial aid.

selection_criteria.academic_excellence: Central to the admission decision, reviewed holistically with no published threshold; it produces no separate merit award because Columbia states there are no merit scholarships.
selection_criteria.leadership: Considered within the holistic admission review; not published as a criterion for aid.
selection_criteria.community_service: Considered within the holistic admission review; not published as a criterion for aid.
selection_criteria.extracurricular_achievement: Considered within the holistic admission review; not published as a criterion for aid.
selection_criteria.financial_need: The sole basis of the award. Eligibility is determined by evaluating the family's ability to pay from total income, parent assets (retirement assets excluded), household size and expenses, number of siblings in undergraduate programmes, and documented special circumstances.
selection_criteria.additional_factors: Fit with the Columbia experience as assessed holistically; rigour of curriculum within the applicant's school system; the Columbia-specific application responses; optional standardised testing for Fall 2027; optional supplementary materials.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree from Columbia College or from Columbia Engineering (The Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science)
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Eight semesters (approximately four years) of full-time study
possible_awards: Bachelor of Science (Columbia College and Columbia Engineering)
degree_outcome.degree_note: The award funds a full bachelor's degree at Columbia College or Columbia Engineering. First-year students are required to live on campus, and the aid is re-assessed each academic year for all four years.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: No advanced-credit or transfer-credit policy for entering first-year students is published on the official pages read for this record, so none is recorded. Columbia requires internal and external examination results (A Level, IB, French Baccalaureate, AP and other final national examinations) to be submitted where they are required to complete and graduate from secondary school.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: The Columbia Grant is applied against the 2026-2027 cost of attendance: tuition $72,800; fees $4,160; food $7,128; housing $12,522; books and supplies $1,320; personal expenses $1,844; travel and local transportation varies; first-year on-campus total $99,774, continuing on-campus total $100,884, living-with-family total $88,060. These figures are the basis for determining financial aid eligibility.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: The $85 nonrefundable application fee applies to all applicants regardless of aid status. Fee waivers are available through the admission application and can be checked in advance with Columbia's fee waiver form.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: No recipient agreement or service obligation is published. Aid recipients are expected to meet the Student Responsibility (Student Contribution plus Student Employment), which may alternatively be covered with outside scholarships, savings, parental assistance or other financing, and enrolled students may apply to the Work Exemption Program for unpaid summer or semester internships.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Financial Aid & Educational Financing (618 Lerner Hall; 212-854-3711; ugrad-finaid@columbia.edu) offers one-on-one guidance on the application process, loans, payment options and budgeting; the International Students & Scholars Office (isso.columbia.edu) supports enrolled international students; Student Financial Services handles billing and the monthly payment plan; the appeals process allows a re-review where family circumstances change or are complex.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No service bond or repayment obligation is published for this award. The Columbia Grant does not need to be repaid, loans are not used to meet need, and Columbia states students are expected to borrow $0 to attend.

application_readiness_checklist: Decide before submitting the admission application whether you are a financial aid applicant - the request cannot be changed later

Confirm you can document your family's income and assets: total income including untaxed income, cash, savings, investments, home equity, other real estate and business equity (retirement assets are excluded)
Complete the CSS Profile and use its Special Circumstances section for anything the standard form cannot convey
Prepare parental tax returns or income documentation for upload to College Board's IDOC
Gather official translations of any non-English transcripts or recommendations, alongside the originals
Line up two teacher recommendations, and for Columbia Engineering one from a math or science teacher
Book an accepted English test early if you do not qualify for an exemption, and have results sent directly (TOEFL report code 2116)
As a low-income international student, email ugrad-finaid@columbia.edu to request a CSS Profile fee waiver
Budget for the Student Responsibility: at least $2,400 summer contribution for most first-years, plus a term-time work expectation of about 7 hours a week
Budget separately for Columbia Health Insurance unless you hold comparable coverage and file the waiver
Plan an optional InitialView or Vericant video by 15 November (Early Decision) or 15 January (Regular Decision) if you want to emphasise fluency
Do not use the Net Price Calculator as an international family - Columbia states it is designed for families living in the US and cannot give an accurate estimate for students living abroad

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The personal essay and the Columbia-specific questions are where the applicant demonstrates intellectual curiosity, habits of mind, love of learning and sense of self. Write concretely about what the applicant would do with Columbia's distinctive experiences in and out of the classroom and why the fit is genuine, rather than recycling generic ambition. Every submitted material must be the applicant's own original work under Columbia's Accuracy and Authenticity statement and its Generative AI Policy.

common_mistakes: Submitting the admission application without declaring financial aid applicant status - the single most consequential error, since the request cannot be changed afterwards
Assuming a strong academic record will produce a merit scholarship - Columbia states none exist
Assuming federal Pell or FAFSA-based aid is available as an international student - it is not; international need is met from institutional resources
Missing the aid paperwork deadlines of 15 November (Early Decision) or 15 February (Regular Decision) and delaying the evaluation
Failing to submit parental tax returns or income documentation through IDOC after the CSS Profile
Using the Net Price Calculator as an international family and treating the estimate as accurate
Not requesting a CSS Profile fee waiver, which low-income international students must request by email

risk_flags.risk: The aid request is irreversible once the admission application is submitted
risk_flags.impact: An international applicant who does not declare financial aid applicant status, or who is admitted without an aid request, can never apply for institutional aid during enrolment unless citizenship status changes; only a severe, unforeseen change in circumstances is reviewed case by case
risk_flags.mitigation: Decide the aid question before submitting the admission application, not after admission, and treat the declaration as final

risk_flags.impact: The admissions committee considers how much aid an applicant requires, so the aid request can itself affect the admission decision, and Early Decision aid applicants may be deferred to Regular Decision
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the two application rounds as strategic choices; do not assume need-blind treatment as an international applicant

risk_flags.risk: Aid is individually calculated, so no amount is guaranteed
risk_flags.impact: The published averages ($79,375 for international recipients, $76,503 average first-year award) cannot be used to budget, and the net cost depends entirely on the family analysis
risk_flags.mitigation: Model the published income bands ($0 parent contribution below $66,000; tuition-free below $150,000) and prepare for the student contribution and work expectation

risk_flags.risk: Student Responsibility remains even for full-need recipients
risk_flags.impact: Most incoming first-year students have a minimum Student Contribution of $2,400 plus a term-time work expectation of about 7 hours a week, so attendance is not cost-free even at $0 parent contribution
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget for the contribution from summer earnings, savings, outside scholarships or parental assistance, and consider the Work Exemption Program after enrolment

risk_flags.risk: Health insurance sits outside the cost of attendance
risk_flags.impact: Students who stay on Columbia Health Insurance pay $2,218 for the Fall term and $3,605 for the Spring term on top of the $99,774 budget unless they file a waiver with comparable coverage
risk_flags.mitigation: Arrange comparable insurance before arriving and file the waiver during the mid-July to end-of-September window

risk_flags.risk: The Net Price Calculator is not valid for international families
risk_flags.impact: Columbia states the calculator is designed for families living in the US and cannot produce an accurate estimate for students living abroad, so self-estimates from it may be badly wrong
risk_flags.mitigation: Contact Financial Aid & Educational Financing directly at ugrad-finaid@columbia.edu for guidance rather than relying on the calculator

risk_flags.risk: Conflicting aggregate figures across official pages
risk_flags.impact: International aid is published as $19 million for 2023-2024 on the admissions page and as $21 million on the same page's fact card; total institutional aid is published as more than $220 million on one page and more than $225 million on another; average first-year awards are $76,503 (admissions) and $70,797 (financial aid office)
risk_flags.mitigation: Record both figures as published and do not treat any of them as current-cycle commitments; re-verify at the 2026-11-01 check

risk_flags.risk: Cycle dates are described as typical rather than fixed
risk_flags.impact: Columbia states its published dates are based on typical admissions cycles and may vary in a particular year, so a dated deadline can drift
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm each date by email to the office before the November and January rounds

database_notes: There is no separately named scholarship to record. Columbia's financial aid office states that all aid it administers is need-based and that there are no academic, athletic or talent-based institutional scholarships, so the programme is recorded under the institutional grant name 'Columbia Grant' with the international-aid framing used by Undergraduate Admissions. No award title is invented.

This target is not on the DO-NOT-DUPLICATE list in research/bachelor/RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md and no Columbia record exists in EXISTING_AWARDS.json, so no substitution was required and the assigned filename was kept. Note that Harvard College, Yale College, MIT and University of Chicago need-based aid records already exist in the database and are explicitly excluded; Columbia is a distinct awarding body.

Columbia's aggregate figures conflict across official pages and both readings are recorded rather than reconciled: international aid is stated as $19 million for 2023-2024 in prose and as $21 million on the same page's fact card; total institutional aid is 'more than $220 million' on the admissions Cost & Aid page and 'more than $225 million' on the financial aid office's Facts and Figures page; the average first-year award is $76,503 (admissions) and the average Columbia grant is $70,797 (financial aid office).

fully_funded is false by design. Columbia meets 100% of demonstrated need and excludes loans from awards, but every recipient still meets a Student Responsibility (a minimum $2,400 Student Contribution for most incoming first-year students plus a term-time work expectation averaging about 7 hours a week), aid is individually assessed rather than universal, the request must be made at admission, and health insurance sits outside the cost of attendance. For families with calculated incomes below $66,000 the parent contribution is $0 and the summer-earnings portion of the student contribution is waived, but a student-assets portion and the work expectation may still apply.

deadline_date is 2026-11-15, the Early Decision financial aid application deadline, because the award's binding dates are the round-specific aid deadlines rather than the admission deadlines. No submission time or timezone is published for these deadlines, so deadline_timezone is null and deadline_precision is 'day'. The Regular Decision aid deadline of 2027-02-15 is recorded in typical_application_window and official_rule.

The two-round structure means single_central_deadline is false: Early Decision applicants have an admission deadline of 1 November and an aid deadline of 15 November 2026, while Regular Decision applicants have an admission deadline of 1 January and an aid deadline of 15 February 2027.

The English proficiency minimums are published as true minimums, not middle-50% ranges, so minimum_ielts (7.5), minimum_toefl (105) and minimum_duolingo (135) are recorded as numbers. TOEFL carries two published minimums because the test changed score scale: 105 for exams taken on or before 20 January 2026 and 5.5 for exams taken on or after 21 January 2026. PTE Academic is not an accepted test, so minimum_pte is null. No score validity period is published, so test_validity_months is null.

The aid application and the admission application are separate submissions with different deadlines, which is recorded explicitly in application_method and application_steps: the aid request is declared on the admission application, but the CSS Profile and IDOC documentation follow afterwards.

The Net Price Calculator is recorded as unusable for this population: Columbia states it is designed for families living in the US and cannot provide an accurate estimate for students living abroad, which matters because this award serves an international applicant pool.

Columbia Health Insurance is deliberately recorded as outside the coverage of the award. It is not part of the cost of attendance, is charged at $2,218 for the Fall term and $3,605 for the Spring term, and can only be waived with comparable insurance during the mid-July to end-of-September window.

Columbia's ISCED level is not stated on any official page read. 'ISCED Level 6 equivalent' is a standard mapping of a U.S. bachelor's degree and is noted here as an interpretation rather than a published fact.

The logo asset is the Columbia crown emblem served from the official Financial Aid & Educational Financing domain (cc-seas.financialaid.columbia.edu). It is small (457 bytes) but is the institution's own mark on its own domain, verified as image/png bytes, and is a dark mark on a light background rather than a white-on-transparent wordmark. A 128-pixel admissions-site favicon is referenced in the admissions page markup but could not be verified as image bytes through a direct request, so it is not used.
